newsitem.title: USA: Calif. average annual pay up 2.8 pct in '95 - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. average annual pay up 2.8 pct in '95 - report.

text.p: Annual pay in California averaged $30,716 in 1995, an increase of 2.8 percent over 1994, U.S. Labor Department said Tuesday.

California's 1995 average annual pay increase of 2.8 percent trailed the national average of 3.4 percent, according to Stanley Stephenson, regional commissioner of the department's bureau of labor statistics.

The 2.8 percent increase compared favorably to the weak 1.4 percent increase measured for California in 1994. California ranked seventh in the nation in 1995, exceeding the national average of $27,845, according to the department.
San Jose posted the largest percentage increase in average annual pay from 1994 to 1995, 8.4 percent, becoming the top ranked city in the nation with a level of $42,409.

In the rest of the region, gains from 1994 to 1995 ranged from 0.1 percent in Alaska to 4.3 percent in Arizona. Pay in the Pacific region averaged $29,112 in 1995, an increase of 3.1 percent over 1994, Labor said.
